newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest weather seen warmer this week - WSC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest weather seen warmer this week - WSC.

text.p: Temperatures in the U.S. Midwest were expected to warm this week but Weather Services Corp meteorologists said cool weather would return next week.
"It looks like it may turn much cooler again next week," said WSC's Joel Burgio. "It looks like any warmer weather we may have this week will be short-lived."
The western Corn Belt will likely remain dry this week, concerning some crop watchers. Cash sources said newly seeded corn and soybeans needed moisture to aid early development.
"I'm not confident that any of the northwest Corn Belt will get rains," Burgio said.
Showers were forecast for Tuesday for Missouri and southern Illinois, with scattered showers and thunderstorms expected late Tuesday and early Wednesday across the southern portions of the belt.
Temperatures were expected to remain just below normal on Monday with highs near 80 degrees Fahrenheit in the northwest to low 70s in the east.
Temperatures should be near normal Tuesday and Wednesday. Normal temperatures for this time of year range from 77 in the northern areas to 82 degrees in the south.
